reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that learning is not a simple stimulus-response mapping but a structured process requiring temporal and spatial alignment of sign, meaning, and outcome. The 'togetherness' principle implies that for any learning event, the sign (S), the means-end relation (M), and the significate (R) must co-vary in a way that allows them to form a perceptual unit. Mathematically, this can be modeled as a conditional probability distribution P(R|S,M) that is non-zero only when S, M, and R are temporally and spatially aligned. The belongingness principle further constrains this by requiring that the elements of the configuration belong together in a meaningful way, which can be formalized as a coherence function C(S,M,R) that must exceed a threshold for learning to occur. The coherent perception kernel ensures that this configuration stands out from the background, implying a signal-to-noise ratio condition. These principles together define a learning kernel K(S,M,R) = C(S,M,R) × P(R|S,M) × P(S,M|R) that governs both Bayesian inference in GSI and state transitions in GSE.
